directive: Mobile-first does not mean tiny. Tactical grid spaces are logical; visual scale must make Deities, Gates, and bosses feel immense.
unitSystem: relativeScaleUnits from world-scale-reference; playerTitan=5.2 reference units
globalRules: Scale sheets must use shared baseline, contact shadows, and at least one mobile crop.
Never shrink deities to solve composition; enlarge Gates, architecture, and battlefield space instead.
Terrain and hazards must be physical art features, never neon board-game overlays.
Every production prompt must preserve dark mythological fantasy and reject sci-fi scale cues.

sheets.title: Normal Enemy vs deity
sheets.composition: Front 3/4 lineup: normal humanoid, standard Hollow enemy, player deity ankle/knee anchor, one standard wall behind.
sheets.camera: Low tactical camera, enemy readable at mobile zoom without stealing deity mass.
promptOverlay: enemy head below deity knee line
qaChecks: Normal enemy never reaches deity waist.
Silhouette stays readable at 360px width.
Wall height remains below deity torso.

sheets.title: Elite Enemy vs deity
sheets.composition: Escalation lineup showing standard enemy, elite enemy, and deity with shared ground plane and contact shadows.
sheets.camera: Slightly lower heroic angle; elite feels threatening but still clearly under deity scale.
promptOverlay: armor mass larger than standard enemy
qaChecks: Elite enemy reads as a deity captain, not a boss.
Deity remains the dominant vertical mass.
Armor volume is larger, not just brighter.

sheets.title: Player deity Hero Scale
sheets.composition: Three deity body classes on one baseline: agile, standard, heavy, with Gate arch ghosted behind.
sheets.camera: Orthographic-friendly side/front comparison plus one action inset for attack arc size.
promptOverlay: Gate arch must tower above all deities
qaChecks: All Deities feel playable at tactical grid scale.
Heavy deity does not become colossal boss scale.
Attack arc extends beyond body silhouette.

sheets.title: Deity-Scale Enemy Duel Reference
sheets.composition: Duel staging: player Deity and deity-scale enemy shoulder-to-shoulder, Gate arch and terrain object in background.
sheets.camera: Boss-preview camera, both silhouettes equally readable with enemy slightly taller or longer-limbed.
qaChecks: Enemy is close enough to duel physically.
Readable counterplay weak points remain visible.
Gate arch still frames both figures above them.

sheets.title: Colossal Boss vs deity
sheets.composition: Player deity foreground at foot/torso line of colossal boss; separate inset shows full boss silhouette against Gate arch.
sheets.camera: Two-panel reference: readable gameplay crop and full majesty silhouette crop.
promptOverlay: Deity reaches lower torso at most
full body must not be cropped in reference inset
qaChecks: Boss feels like a battlefield event, not a large elite.
Gameplay crop keeps attack telegraphs readable.
Mobile boss zoom preserves objective UI space.

sheets.title: Mythos Gate Landmark Scale
sheets.composition: Gate arch, inner opening, Deity, and colossal boss silhouettes aligned on the same threshold stones.
sheets.camera: Wide landmark camera with clear inner passage and readable threshold material detail.
qaChecks: Gate is visible as a landmark from battlefield camera.
Inner opening exceeds deity height.
Architecture avoids sci-fi portal framing.

sheets.title: Architecture and Cover Scale
sheets.composition: Temple pylon, wall, statue, bridge width markers, and deity placed on shared tactical floor tiles.
sheets.camera: Isometric tactical camera with lane/cover readability and no artificial grid glow.
promptOverlay: cover can hide enemies but not Deities
qaChecks: Architecture makes Deities feel immense without clipping them.
Cover is readable as gameplay terrain.
No modern/sci-fi scale cues appear.

sheets.title: Interactive Battlefield Object Scale
sheets.composition: Solar seal pylon, fallen gate rib, breakable wall, and objective pedestal beside deity feet and normal enemies.
sheets.camera: Mobile combat zoom focused on tap targets, obstruction, and silhouette separation.
promptOverlay: objective pedestal below deity knee but above normal enemy waist
qaChecks: Tap target is visible at 360x640.
Object silhouette is separate from enemy silhouettes.
Terrain effects are embedded in art, not neon overlays.
